summary: The implementation is biologically acceptable within the claim's limited scope as apparent central-body mask width. Comparative-mode logic keeps unusual length, width, ratio, curvature, slice span, and warning-only morphology in the technical-valid population; WT reference morphology remains diagnostic rather than an acceptance or tuning rule. Representative width is selected from an observed valid-width plane without choosing the widest plane or fabricating missing values. Reporting explicitly limits the metric to segmentation-derived apparent width and does not support molecular diameter, whole-organ volume, or genotype inference. Confidence is medium because focused tests could not be rerun in the managed read-only environment and the retained biological evidence contains only one specimen per group.

Source inspection and the commit-bound validation receipt were therefore used instead of claiming a current test rerun.

findings.title: Width is a segmentation-derived apparent phenotype
findings.impact: The measurement can support descriptive apparent-width comparisons under matched acquisition and segmentation conditions, but it cannot establish true chromatin diameter or prove that an observed difference is biological rather than boundary, focus, annotation, or PSF variation.
evidence: audits/claims_registry.json:105-111 lists segmentation boundary, focus, annotation thickness, lateral PSF, and lack of molecular-scale interpretation as limitations.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:7382-7387 explicitly disclaims a mathematically PSF-corrected physical diameter.
audits/evidence/v571_body_width_final/body_width_visual_evidence_manifest.json:11 states the same measurement limitation.
findings.recommendation: Continue using the terms apparent body width and mask width. Require blinded manual-mask agreement across representative morphologies and external optical validation before making accuracy or true-diameter claims.

findings.title: Current specimens cannot support a genotype conclusion
findings.impact: The retained KJ and WT examples validate execution and plausibility only; they are not independent replication sufficient for between-group inference.

limitations: No full image stack was run, as required by the review instructions.
The focused pytest invocation could not start because the managed read-only environment exposed no usable temporary directory.
Synthetic coverage supports short, long, wide, thin, curved, low-ratio, single-slice, fragmented-looking, and fused-looking behavior but is not external biological validation.
No blinded independent manual-mask dataset establishes agreement across the full morphology range.
The retained biological evidence includes only one independent specimen per group.
The measurement remains conditional on the filled U-Net boundary and centerline and is not optical deconvolution or molecular-scale validation.
recommended_follow_up: Compare apparent body width with blinded manual masks across short, long, wide, thin, curved, fragmented-looking, fused-looking, single-slice, and low-ratio nuclei.
Report width availability and missingness per specimen to detect morphology-dependent failure to obtain sufficient chord samples.
Use multiple independent WT and mutant specimens, with specimen-level inference.
Keep molecular diameter and anatomical whole-organ volume outside this claim unless supported by external optical validation and slice-specific 3D organ masks.
